name: Semantic Equivalence Masking via Constraint Satisfaction
description: The problem is reframed from explicitly checking for a 3-clique ('any two materials chosen from the set correspond to a prohibited pair') to an equivalent constraint satisfaction property ('impossible to assign them to two vessels'). Surface pattern matchers will fixate on the 'two vessels' framing and attempt to deploy generic bipartite-checking or 2-SAT algorithms (like BFS for odd cycles), which struggle to efficiently enforce the exact subset size of 3 and the strict lexicographical minimization. Genuine reasoners will deduce that a 3-variable 2-coloring fails if and only if it is a 3-clique, and will confidently implement the correct, efficient triangle-enumerating algorithm.
